Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed spike: region eu-west-1 between 09:00 and 09:20 UTC, aligned with the customer's timestamps.
- Symptom: elevated 504s at the streaming proxy level and client-side socket CLOSE_AFTER_TIMEOUT. Backend runtime shows no OOMs or model worker failures.
- Likely cause: sudden burst of concurrent streams with larger-than-average prompt/response sizes caused proxy buffer backpressure. We also shipped a small runtime change in last night's deploy (2026-08-23 22:45 UTC) that adjusted chunk coalescing heuristics for efficiency — that may have increased variance in chunk size and delayed flushes under high concurrency.

What I need from Brightline: a short list of concurrent users, average message size, and any custom client keepalive settings. Jonas — please pull proxy-trace file and NGINX error logs for 09:00-09:20. I'll check the deploy changelist and roll back if we confirm a regression.

Subject: Re: Live demo - repeated chunked-transfer timeouts (URGENT)

Update from runtime investigation:
- Root cause: confirmed. The streaming proxy's buffer allocator became saturated when handling a burst of ~180 concurrent streams from Brightline during the window. A regression in chunk coalescing (deploy 2026-08-23) led to uneven chunk emission: some streams emitted very large chunks while others had long idle gaps. The combination caused NGINX upstream buffers to hit limits and trigger timeout closes on clients.
- Repro: we replayed a synthetic workload that simulates Brightline's traffic and reliably reproduced the stall within the same config.

Mitigations applied (done by 13:00 UTC Tues):
1) Hotfix: reverted the chunk coalescing change in runtime and promoted a small rollback to eu-west-1.
2) Proxy config: increased proxy_buffer_size and lowered proxy_read_timeout to reduce long-tail stalls.
3) Customer mitigation: enabled polling fallback for Brightline sessions for the short term (avoids long-lived sockets).

Follow-ups (planned):
- Patch: a deterministic chunking fix (PR 4281) to prevent uneven emission. Link: https://redwood-internal/github/redwood/runtime/pulls/4281
- Load-safety: add a regional throttle circuit to protect proxies when client concurrency spikes unexpectedly.
- Telemetry: add a dashboard for chunk-size distribution and proxy buffer saturation alerts.

I'm recommending a postmortem and an executive summary for Brightline. Monica — can you coordinate customer-facing language and credits? Vanessa — I can be on the call with execs.

-Jonas
Senior Staff Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: RESOLVED: Brightline streaming timeouts — executive summary and next steps

Sara / Tom / Team —

Thank you for your patience. Below is an executive summary of what happened, what we did, and our commitments.

Incident summary:
- Window: 2026-08-24 09:00–09:20 UTC (eu-west-1) during a Brightline demo.
- Impact: increased token delivery latency and chunked-transfer/websocket timeouts causing partial responses and a degraded demo experience. Error rate for the session peaked ~8%.

Root cause:
- A recent runtime optimization (2026-08-23 deploy) changed chunk coalescing behavior. Under a burst of concurrent streams from Brightline (~180 concurrent sessions), chunk emission became uneven and caused regional proxy buffer exhaustion, followed by timeouts.

Actions taken:
- Immediate rollback of the coalescing change in eu-west-1 (mitigated the immediate stalls).
- Increased regional proxy buffer configurations and adjusted timeouts to reduce tail closes.
- Enabled polling fallback for affected Brightline sessions while we test the deterministic chunking fix.
- Issued a temporary credit for the impacted demo window (details via Monica).

Commitments and next steps:
- Fix: runtime PR 4281 (deterministic-chunking) is under review; target staged rollout by 2026-08-31.
- Safety: implement regional concurrency circuit and alerting for proxy buffer saturation by 2026-09-10.
- Postmortem: full postmortem and telemetry graphs will be shared by 2026-08-30.
- Customer: we will schedule an exec sync to review the PMA and remediation plan; Monica will propose times.

Apology: We know this impacted your demo and are sorry. Our goal is predictable, demo-grade performance for POCs — and we missed that. We will make this right.

—Vanessa Ortiz
